<Phase type="activation">

Picture a hotel that sells rooms only a whole floor at a time. Every evening the floor is paid for, even if half the rooms are dark.

**The owner is at ease. Whoever bought the floor is not.** Think about how long they will keep buying floors from this hotel.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the dark windows. The venue's guaranteed revenue is someone's risk that has not gone anywhere.

**The rate model decides who carries the empty places.** A model that is too rigid protects the venue today and scares leaders off tomorrow.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## Three models in one calculator

The academy calculator also shows the deal through the venue's eyes — the view switch is at the top. Take one and the same week: 6 nights, a guest price of 3,000 dollars, a venue rate of 1,800 per guest.

**A full campus for 20, 12 came** — [open](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#). The venue gets 36,000 dollars whatever the number of guests. The leader is 1,080 in the red.

**Per guest, minimum 14, 12 came** — [open](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#). The venue gets 25,200: a minimum of 14 guests at the rate. The leader earns 9,720.

**Buyout, 16 guests** — [open](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#). The venue gets 20,000 for the dates and 600 per guest for meals, 29,600 in total. The leader earns 16,960.

## What the venue chooses

A full campus gives the venue the most predictable revenue. But it shifts all the risk of a short group onto the leader. A new leader with a small audience will often not dare to take such a model, or will lose money and not come back.

Per-guest pricing with a minimum shares the risk. The minimum protects the venue from a very small group, and the leader does not pay for every empty bed.

A buyout suits a small venue or one let as a whole. It is a fee for the dates plus an extra charge per guest for food and services.

There is also a soft entry for new leaders: a free place for the leader once the group reaches a threshold. The venue invests one place in a relationship with a leader who already has their own audience.

## What the package includes

The venue's rate is worth spelling out: accommodation, linen and cleaning, halls, meals, transfers, equipment. What is not on the list is not in the package. An unclear package is a reason for an argument on site.

<SelfCheck id="c1"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the three teaching deals through the links above and switch the calculator to the venue's view.
2. For each, write down how much the venue gets and how much the leader gets.
3. Work out under which model it pays for the leader to come back to you next year.
4. List your package: what is included in the rate, what costs extra.
5. Choose the model and the minimum you are ready to offer a new leader.

</Phase>
